title: Choosing and Combining Discrete Probability Models

questions.title: Model Identification: Binomial versus Geometric
questions.scenario:
A student conducts two separate probability experiments using a fair six-sided die, numbered 1 to 6.
In Experiment 1, the die is rolled 10 times, and the total number of sixes obtained is denoted by $X$.
In Experiment 2, the die is rolled repeatedly until a six is obtained for the first time, and the number of rolls required is denoted by $Y$.

parts.text: State the standard probability distribution of $X$, including its parameters, and state the standard probability distribution of $Y$, including its parameter.

questions.title: Parameter Estimation and Variance in Binomial Models
questions.scenario: A random variable $X$ is modeled by a binomial distribution $B(n, p)$. A sample of $n = 50$ trials is observed, and the mean number of successes is $E(X) = 14$.

parts.text: Calculate the value of $p$ and determine the variance $\text{Var}(X)$.

questions.title: Geometric Mean and Point Probability
questions.scenario: A random variable $X$ represents the number of independent trials required to obtain the first success in an experiment where the probability of success on each trial is $p = 0.16$.

parts.text: Calculate the expected value $E(X)$ and find $P(X = 4)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Distribution of Score Difference on Two Dice
questions.scenario: Two fair four-sided dice, each with faces numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, are rolled simultaneously. The random variable $D$ represents the positive difference between the two numbers shown, that is, $D = |S_1 - S_2|$.

parts.text: Construct the probability distribution table of $D$ and calculate the expected value $E(D)$.

questions.title: Fixed-Position Event: The Second Defect
questions.scenario: A manufacturing machine produces items of which $20\%$ are defective. Items are inspected one by one in a random sequence. The inspections are independent.

parts.text: Find the probability that the 5th item inspected is the 2nd defective item found.

questions.title: Triggered Multi-Stage Model: Spinner and Coin
questions.scenario:
A game uses a fair spinner with four sectors numbered 1, 2, 3, 4. A player spins the spinner once to obtain a score $N$.
The player then tosses a fair coin $N$ times. Let $H$ be the number of heads obtained.

parts.text: Calculate the probability that the spinner lands on 3 and the player obtains exactly 2 heads.

questions.title: Comparing Monitoring Protocols: Binomial and Geometric
questions.scenario:
A telecommunications company tests calls to customer support. On any given call, the probability that the caller is placed on hold for more than two minutes is $0.35$. Calls are independent.
The supervisor compares two monitoring protocols:
- Under Protocol A, a supervisor monitors a random sample of 12 calls and records the number of calls $X$ that are on hold for more than two minutes.
- Under Protocol B, a supervisor monitors calls one after another until a call is on hold for more than two minutes, and records the total number of calls $Y$ monitored.

parts.text: State the distribution of $X$, and calculate the probability that exactly 4 calls in the sample of 12 are on hold for more than two minutes.
State the distribution of $Y$, and calculate the probability that the supervisor under Protocol B monitors exactly 4 calls.

questions.title: Sampling Without Replacement and Discrete Tables
questions.scenario:
A box contains 3 cards numbered 1, 2, and 3. Two cards are drawn at random without replacement.
Let $S$ be the sum of the numbers on the two chosen cards.

parts.text: Explain why $S$ cannot be modeled by a binomial distribution, and construct the probability distribution table for $S$.
Calculate the expected value $E(S)$ and the variance $\text{Var}(S)$.

questions.title: Triggered Multi-Stage Trials and Total Probability
questions.scenario:
A game is played in two stages.
In Stage 1, a player spins a fair spinner with 3 equal sectors numbered 1, 2, and 3. The number obtained is denoted by $N$.
In Stage 2, the player tosses a fair coin $N$ times. The total number of heads obtained is denoted by $H$.

parts.text: Calculate the joint probability $P(N = 3 \cap H = 2)$.
Calculate the total probability that the number of heads obtained is equal to the number spun on the spinner, that is, $P(H = N)$.

questions.title: Extended Waiting Times: Higher-Order Defect Positions
questions.scenario: Components produced on an automated assembly line have an independent probability of $0.15$ of being defective. An inspector tests components one by one as they come off the line.

parts.text: Find the probability that the 7th component tested is the 2nd defective component found.
Find the probability that the 8th component tested is the 3rd defective component found.

questions.title: Geometric Intervals and Reliability Thresholds
questions.scenario:
A computer system transmits data packets over a noisy channel. The probability that any packet is successfully transmitted on a single attempt is $0.18$. Packet transmissions are independent.
Let $X$ be the number of attempts required to achieve the first successful transmission.

parts.text: Calculate the probability that the number of attempts required to achieve the first successful transmission is strictly between 3 and 8, that is, $P(3 < X < 8)$.
Find the smallest number of attempts $n$ such that the probability of achieving at least one successful transmission in $n$ attempts is greater than $0.98$.

questions.title: Multi-Model Dice Tournament: Geometric Waiting and Binomial Counting
questions.scenario:
Two fair four-sided dice, each with faces numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, are rolled together in a sequence of games.
In each game, let $D = |S_1 - S_2|$ be the absolute difference between the scores.
A game is defined as a "success" if $D \ge 2$.

parts.text: Show that the probability of success in a single game is $\frac{3}{8}$.

The dice are rolled repeatedly until a success ($D \ge 2$) is achieved. Let $W$ be the number of games played up to and including the first success. Find $E(W)$ and calculate $P(W \le 3)$, expressing your answer as an exact fraction.

In a separate tournament, 10 independent games are played. Let $Y$ be the number of games that result in a success ($D \ge 2$). Find the probability that at least 3 of the 10 games result in a success.

questions.title: Comprehensive Quality Assurance: Binomial, Geometric, and Fixed Position
questions.scenario: A microchip manufacturing plant tests silicon wafers. Each wafer has an independent probability of $0.10$ of containing a critical defect.

parts.text: In a quality audit, a random sample of 20 wafers is inspected. Let $X$ be the number of defective wafers in the sample. Calculate the mean and variance of $X$, and find the probability that exactly 2 wafers in the sample are defective.

Wafers are now tested one by one until the first defective wafer is found. Let $T$ be the number of wafers tested. Find $P(T > 8)$, and determine the least number of wafers $m$ that must be tested so that the probability of finding at least one defective wafer is greater than $0.95$.
In a continuous production run, wafers are inspected sequentially until a second defective wafer is found. Calculate the probability that exactly 10 wafers are tested in total.
